name: β-funaltrexamine
summary: β-Funaltrexamine (β-FNA) is an irreversible (covalently bonding) opioid antagonist that was used to create the first crystal structure of the μ-opioid receptor (MOR). It is selective for antagonism of the MOR over the δ-opioid receptor (DOR) and κ-opioid receptor (KOR). Chemically, it is a naltrexone derivative with a methyl-fumaramide group in the 6-position.

pharmacology.text: β-Funaltrexamine (β-FNA) is an irreversible (covalently bonding) opioid antagonist that was used to create the first crystal structure of the μ-opioid receptor (MOR). It is selective for antagonism of the MOR over the δ-opioid receptor (DOR) and κ-opioid receptor (KOR).

uses.text: β-Funaltrexamine (β-FNA) is an irreversible (covalently bonding) opioid antagonist that was used to create the first crystal structure of the μ-opioid receptor (MOR).

sideEffects.en: It is a laboratory tool and has not been studied in people. Opioid antagonists given to someone dependent on opioids can cause sudden, severe withdrawal.
sideEffects.zh: 它是實驗室工具，未曾在人體研究過。對鴉片類成癮者使用鴉片受體拮抗劑可能引發突發而嚴重的戒斷反應。
sideEffects.zhHans: 它是实验室工具，未曾在人体研究过。对鸦片类成瘾者使用鸦片受体拮抗剂可能引发突发而严重的戒断反应。

fact.en: It latches on to the mu-opioid receptor permanently, forming a chemical bond. That is what let scientists hold the receptor still long enough to work out the first crystal structure of it.
fact.zh: 它會與 μ 鴉片受體形成化學鍵而永久附著。正是這一點讓科學家能把受體固定得足夠久，從而解出它的第一個晶體結構。
fact.zhHans: 它会与 μ 鸦片受体形成化学键而永久附着。正是这一点让科学家能把受体固定得足够久，从而解出它的第一个晶体结构。
